title: self
goal: In this lesson you will learn that self means this object inside a method.
learn: self is the object calling the method
Use self.attr to read or change data
You do not pass self yourself when calling
idea: Inside a method, self means this object. The one before the dot. When you write dog.bark(), Python sends dog into self automatically. Use self.name to reach that object's attributes. You do not type self in the call.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change starting age to 5. Press Run. Birthday line should say is now 6.

practice.text: In shout, print self.name in all caps message. Call it.
practice.hint: self.name is "Sam" on f. You can print a loud message with self.name inside. Try .upper() on the name for ALL CAPS.
practice.starterTip: print(self.name.upper(), "cheers!") or print("GO", self.name.upper() + "!") inside shout.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if shout uses self.name in the print.

practice.text: Finish deposit so it adds amount to self.balance. Show before/after.
practice.hint: Inside deposit, update self.balance by adding amount to the old balance. After b.deposit(5), print(b.balance) should show 15.
practice.starterTip: self.balance = self.balance + amount. Same idea as the PiggyBank lesson.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if balance becomes 15 via self.balance update.

options.text: The object that called the method

quiz.question: Do you pass self when calling dog.bark()?

options.text: No. Python fills self for you
